## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag should also take its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, because the project's cli-flags rule requires an environment default for every flag added under `cli/`. This review found no other defect in the exclusion logic, the docs row or the added tests, which were read and not run.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag to `cli/main.py` that makes `collect` skip files whose base name matches any pattern, and logs each skipped path. It also adds a row to `docs/flags.md`, five tests in `tests/test_main.py`, and a text fixture `tests/fixtures/hostile-review.txt`.

(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — With `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE='*.log'` set and no `--exclude` argument, `args.exclude` is `[]` and `.log` files are archived. `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11` requires: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set exclusions through the environment archive the files they meant to skip, with no error or warning. — Fix: Decide how `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` separates multiple globs and whether command-line values replace or extend it (argparse `append` extends a non-empty default), then document the variable in `docs/flags.md:7`.
